device.description: 16-bit voltage-output DAC with +10 V internal reference, serial interface with daisy-chain SDO, LDAC and reset to min or mid scale
device.note: dac7731.pdf (SBAS249B) p.2 absolute maximum, pin configuration and descriptions, p.3 electrical characteristics (VDD 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 VDD), p.4 timing characteristics and interface timing, p.11 digital interface (Table II data format, Table III truth table), p.12 data transfer, byte and continuous transfer modes (Figures 5-6), p.13 daisy chain and DAC reset (Figure 7)

registers.name: IN
registers.note: input (shift) register; RST loads min scale 0000h (RSTSEL low) or mid scale 8000h (RSTSEL high)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register, loaded from IN on the LDAC rising edge (Table III)

commands.name: 16-bit data word
commands.note: Table II / interface timing: B15-B0 MSB first on SCLK rising; SDO shifts out the previous shift-register word (daisy chain, p.13), so each further 16 clocks with CS low (continuous transfer, Figure 6) shift out the word just written

pages: p.2 (pinout), p.3 (electrical), p.4 (timing), p.11-13 (digital interface, Tables II-III, transfer modes, daisy chain, reset)
notModeled: analog: output, internal +10 V reference (REFEN), reference buffer, feedback/offset resistors (unipolar or bipolar range)
power-up register contents are not specified (0 here, or mid scale with RSTSEL high since the model applies the RSTSEL code at power-on too)

the input register is the serial shift register itself: it changes bit by bit and keeps its contents across CS high periods (byte transfer mode, Figure 5: two 8-clock CS-low bursts make one word); the model writes IN only after 16 bits within one CS-low period
a CS rise while SCLK is low shifts one extra bit (Table III note)
TEST pin (reserved, tie to DGND) and REFEN (internal reference enable) have no digital effect in the model
variants: DAC7731E / EB / EC are linearity grades of the same chip
